prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Your Pet is Getting Ready!", "Feed your pet snacks while your desktop environment compiles."]
1: []
2: ["Choose Your Perfect Desktop Companion", "Select a friend to join you on your desktop workspace."]
3: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Pet Workspace!", "Your pet is now active on your desktop."]
4: ["Compiling 3D desktop assets and behaviors..."]
5: ["Sign In to Restore Your Saved Pets & Purchases", "Log into your account to automatically load existing desktop pets, customizations, and settings."]
6: ["You can minimize this window. We'll alert you on your desktop as soon as your pet is ready!"]
7: ["Your Recommended Desktop Friends", "Based on your quiz answers, here are the best companion matches for your workflow."]
8: ["Setup Complete! Claim Your Free Desktop Wallpapers", "Your pet is live! Enjoy your exclusive custom desktop wallpaper gift bundle."]
9: ["Don't worry — you can easily change your path settings or switch companions anytime in desktop preferences."]
